text: In a circle, the angle at the center is double that at the circumference, when the angles have the same circumference base. Let $ABC$ be a circle, and let $BEC$ be an angle at its center, and $BAC$ (one) at (its) circumference. And let them have the same circumference base $BC$. I say that angle $BEC$ is double (angle) $BAC$.
For being joined, let $AE$ be drawn through to $F$.
Therefore, since $EA$ is equal to $EB$, angle $EAB$ (is) also equal to $EBA$ [Prop.~1.5].

assertion: the sum of angles EAB and EBA is double angle EAB
angle BEF equals angle EAB plus angle EBA
angle BEF is double angle EAB

text: So, for the same (reasons), $FEC$ is also double $EAC$.
assertion: angle FEC is double angle EAC

text: Thus, the whole (angle) $BEC$ is double the whole (angle) $BAC$.
assertion: angle BEC is double angle BAC (case 1)
